Authors: C. Paduraru; M. Cernat; A. -N. Staicu
Author Affiliations: Department of Computer Science, University of Bucharest, Romania; Department of Computer Science, University of Bucharest, Romania; Department of Computer Science, University of Bucharest, Romania
Publication Title: 2023 27th International Conference on Engineering of Complex Computer Systems (ICECCS)
Abstract: By using Robotic Process Automation (RPA), repetitive processes in companies can be automated and executed with intelligent software agents. These agents are able to run such processes without human effort and with less error-proneness. RPA has gained significant traction in recent years and is being used by many companies to reduce internal costs and achieve a higher return on investment (ROI). In our literature review, we found that there is a gap in the testability of RPA workflows. In this paper, we focus on addressing this gap using concolic execution (also referred to as online symbolic execution in the literature). First, we explore how previous work in the literature on concolic execution can be reused for the RPA domain and we implement a prototype. Then, we evaluate our open source solution for adapting concolic execution to the RPA context, using real-world use cases and best practices.

Document Title: Design and Implementation of a Hybrid Ontology-NLP Autonomous Web Agent for Intelligent Information Interaction
Author Affiliations: School of Computer Science and Engineering, Lovely Professional University, Phagwara, Punjab; School of Computer Science and Engineering, Lovely Professional University, Phagwara, Punjab
Publication Title: 2026 5th OPJU International Technology Conference (OTCON) on Smart Computing for Innovation and Advancement in Industry 5.0
Abstract: The next generation of the intelligent adaptive and user centric web interaction is now taking the form of autonomous web agents. Although ontology based agents are more semantically precise and explainable, they are frequently not flexible to natural language inputs. In contrast, NLP motivated models are not only flexible linguistically, but are black box systems with poor transparency. This paper discusses the design and implementation of a hybrid ontology, NLP autonomous web agent which involves combination of symbolic reasoning with language understanding in order to acquire both interpretability and contextual adaptability. The system architecture integrates semantic validation in the form of SPARQL reasoning and rule based planning with natural language intent recognition and entity extraction. The suitability of the approach is confirmed with a prototype of the proof-of-concept healthcare questionanswering that works with the publicly available MedQuAD benchmark. According to experimental findings, the success rate in the tasks, semantic consistency, and the explanation are better than those of standalone ontology or NLP based models. The suggested hybrid system offers a useful basis for credible, areaconscientious, and classifiable autonomous representatives in Web 4.0 ecosystems.
